 Texas A&M QB Brady Hart has had opportunities to prove he’s ready for more playing time 
 KBTX News at Ten(Recurring) By Travis L. Brown Published : Nov. 2, 2026 at 6:05 PM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google COLLEGE STATION, Texas (KBTX) - Texas A&M backup quarterback Brady Hart has been given plenty of chances in practice to prove he is ready for an added workload on Saturdays, head coach Mike Elko said during his weekly press conference Monday.
 However, Marcel Reed continues to be the Aggies’ starter heading into a 2 p.m. bout Saturday at South Carolina and is “the right thing to do for us to win on Saturday’s,” Elko confirmed last week during an SEC coaches teleconference.
 “We feel like Brady gets a ton of opportunities to showcase where he’s at, a ton of opportunities to show us whether or not he’s ready to go or step in and be the guy,” Elko said Monday. “The challenge to him has been, if you want opportunities, there’s a level that we need to see in order to feel comfortable about doing that.”
 Elko and his staff were close to making a switch at quarterback in the first quarter of A&M’s road trip to Alabama, after Reed threw two interceptions in his first three pass attempts. However, the four-year veteran found a rhythm through the second and third quarters that kept the Aggies in the game. A 9-yard passing touchdown from Reed to wide receiver Mario Craver in the first quarter and a 4-yard rushing touchdown by Reed in the second are the only two touchdowns the Aggies have tallied on the road this season.
 After the open week, Reed ranks 142nd in Pro Football Focus passing grades among 171 quarterbacks who have played at least 20% of 283 dropbacks this season at 57.6. Eight power conference quarterbacks have graded worse this season: Tait Reynolds (Clemson), Nico Iamaleava (UCLA), Colton Joseph (Wisconsin), John Mateer (Oklahoma), Alonza Burnett III (UCF), Julian Lewis (Colorado), Parker Puckett (Mississippi State) and Faizon Brandon (Tennessee).
 Of those eight, five have been replaced by a backup quarterback. UCF’s Burnett and UCLA’s Iamaleava were replaced due to injury.
 Reed has completed 56.8% of his passes, which ranks 19th among 20 quarterbacks in the SEC, for 1,388 yards, 14th among 38 qualifying SEC quarterbacks, and eight passing touchdowns, tied for 13th among 38 qualifying SEC quarterbacks. He has thrown eight interceptions, which is tied for 17th among 20 qualifying SEC quarterbacks.
 Hart, a sophomore, has played 61 snaps this season in which he’s completed 57.1% of his passes for 143 yards and two passing touchdowns. He also threw an interception in his first attempt at the end of A&M’s loss at LSU.
 Elko said there hasn’t been a need for Hart to get increased first-team reps, because of how A&M structures its practices. Members of both the first and second teams rotate in and out frequently, forming what Elko called 1 1/2 reps.
 “We’re probably more balanced than most people in terms of how we rep things, and so, for us, we don’t have that ones and twos thing the way other people talk about it,” Elko said. “I don’t think they do either. I Think they just say things. Because, when the wideouts run a post, they don’t come back and run another post. The next group of wideouts goes in. Or, your running back breaks off a 20-yard run, the next running back goes in.”
 However, pieces of A&M’s performance in the Aggies’ 31-20 loss at Alabama give the head coach confidence his team can have a more successful November, Elko said Monday.
 “I thought there were times in that Alabama game where we played football the way we’d like to,” Elko said. “I thought the physicality has taken some steps forward on both sides of the line of scrimmage. I thought we did a better job against them stopping the run, running the football. Through the second and third quarters of that game, I thought offensive efficiency was as good as it’s been. We didn’t finish the game, obviously, the way we would have wanted to and didn’t get it done in the fourth quarter the way we needed to, to be successful, but I think some of the growth is there.”
 A&M averaged 130.125 yards per first half this season coming into the Alabama game. The Aggies posted 174 before halftime in that game, including a 2-for-4 clip on third down. The Aggies were also 3-for-3 in the red zone in that first half.
 In the third quarter of that game, the Aggie defense held Alabama to nine rushing yards on four attempts. Of Alabama’s 34 total rushing yards in the fourth quarter, 29 came on the final drive of the game as the Crimson Tide attempted to milk the remainder of the clock.
 Run defense will be a focus of Saturday’s game in South Carolina, as the Gamecocks enter the contest ranked first in the SEC in rushing yards per game, averaging 217.5.
 The Aggies then face No. 16 Tennessee, Oklahoma and No. 10 Texas to close out the season, searching for two wins to become bowl eligible.
 “We’re not talking about growth when we’re not winning football games, because that’s what we’re here to do, but I do think there are signs that progress is being made,” Elko said. “We’ve got to make it faster, more, bigger in order to get the results that we want.”
